Methodology  
Selected Bank of America transaction data is used to inform the macroeconomic views expressed in this report and should be considered in the 
context of other economic indicators and publicly available information. In certain instances, the data may provide directional and/or predictive 
value. The data used is not comprehensive; it is based on aggregated and anonymized selections of Bank of America data and may reflect a 
degree of selection bias and limitations on the data available. 
Any payments data represents aggregated spend from US Retail, Preferred, Small Business and Wealth Management clients with a deposit 
account or credit card. Aggregated spend include total credit card, debit card, ACH, wires, bill pay, business/peer-to-peer, cash, and checks.  
Any Small Business payments data represents aggregate spend from Small Business clients with a deposit account or a Small Business credit 
card. Payroll payments data include channels such as ACH (automated clearing house), bill pay, checks and wire. Bank of America per Small 
Business client data represents activity spending from active Small Business clients with a deposit account or a Small Business credit card and 
at least one transaction in each month. Small businesses in this report include business clients within Bank of America and generally defined as 
under $5mm in annual sales revenue.  
Unless otherwise stated, data is not adjusted for seasonality, processing days or portfolio changes, and may be subject to periodic revisions.  
The differences between the total and per household card spending growth rate (if discussed) can be explained by the following reasons:  
1. Overall total card spending growth is partially boosted by the growth in the number of active cardholders in our sample. This could be due to 
an increasing customer base or inactive customers using their cards more frequently. 
2. Per household card spending growth only looks at households that complete at least five transactions with Bank of America cards in the 
month. Per household spending growth isolates impacts from a changing sample size, which could be unrelated to underlying economic 
momentum, and potential spending volatility from less active users. 
3. Overall total card spending includes small business card spending while per household card spending does not. 
4. Differences due to using processing dates (total card spending) versus transaction date (per household card spending). 
5. Other differences including household formations due to young adults moving in and out of their parent’s houses during COVID. 
Any household consumer deposit data based on Bank of America internal data is derived by anonymizing and aggregating data from Bank of 
America consumer deposit accounts in the US and analyzing that data at a highly aggregated level. Whenever median household savings and 
checking balances are quoted, the data is based on a fixed cohort of households that had a consumer deposit account (checking and/or savings 
account) for all months from January 2019 through the most current month of data shown.  
Bank of America aggregated credit/debit card spending per household includes spending from active US households only. Only consumer card 
holders making a minimum of five transactions a month are included in the dataset. Spending from corporate cards are excluded. Data 
regarding merchants who receive payments are identified and classified by the Merchant Categorization Code (MCC) defined by financial 
services companies. The data are mapped using proprietary methods from the MCCs to the North American Industry Classification System 
(NAICS), which is also used by the Census Bureau, in order to classify spending data by subsector. Spending data may also be classified by other 
proprietary methods not using MCCs.  
Store category aggregation for “more discretionary”, “partly discretionary”, and “mostly necessity” is defined as follows: 
More discretionary: furniture, electronics, building materials, hobbies, miscellaneous stores, nonstore retail, clothing. 
Partly discretionary: auto, health and personal care, general merchandise. 
Mostly necessity: Gasoline, food and beverage.  
We consider a measure of services necessity spending that includes but is not limited to groceries, utilities, and gasoline. Discretionary services 
includes but is not limited to charitable donations, leisure travel, entertainment, and professional/consumer services. Discretionary retail 
includes but is not limited to general merchandise, miscellaneous, clothing, electronics and furniture. It excludes categories like groceries and 
gasoline. Holiday spending is defined as items in which spending in the November-December period is usually at least 20% of total annual 
spending on the category.  Value and premium grocers are determined judgmentally on a proprietary analysis of merchants by equity analysts. 
The “more discretionary” retail category includes furniture, electronics, building materials, online marketplaces, clothing retailers and 
miscellaneous stores; while “partly discretionary” retail contains auto parts and services, health and personal care retailers, general merchandise 
and “mostly necessity”  retail contains gas and groceries. 
Lower, middle and higher household income cuts in Bank of America credit and debit card spending per household, and consumer deposit 
account data are based on quantitative estimates of each households’ income. These quantitative estimates are bucketed according to terciles, 
with a third of households placed in each tercile periodically. The lowest tercile represents ‘lower income’, the middle tercile represents ‘middle 
income’ and the highest tercile ‘higher income’. The income thresholds between these terciles will move over time, reflecting any number of 
factors that impact income, including general wage inflation, changes in social security payments and individual households’ income. The 
income and tercile in which a household is categorised are periodically re-assessed.  
Generations, if discussed, are defined as follows: Gen Z, born after 1995; Younger Millennials: born between 1989-1995; Older Millennials: born 
between 1978-1988; Gen Xers: born between 1965-1977; Baby Boomer: 1946-1964; Traditionalists: pre-1946. 
Any reference to card spending per household on gasoline includes all purchases at gasoline stations and might include purchases of non-gas 
items. 
Additional information about the methodology used to aggregate the data is available upon request.

#inflation #newzealand
First Impressions: NZ Consumers Price Index Q3 2026 and change
of OCR call
By Satish Ranchhod
Senior Economist, Westpac NZ
09:19 October 22 2026 Share
Consumer prices rose 0.7% in the September quarter and 3.7% y/y. Core inflation
pressures are elevated and market pricing is primed for a 25bp OCR hike next week, which
we now expect.
Consumers Price Index, September quarter 2026 – key stats

### Page 2

Headline inflation

RBNZ: +0.8%
Market median: +0.8%, range +0.5% to +1.2%

Quarterly change: +0.2% (prev: +2.7%)

Consumer prices rose 0.7% in the September quarter. That saw the annual inflation rate easing to
3.7%, down from 4.1% in the year to June. 
Today’s result was in line with our forecast, but lower than the RBNZ’s forecast for 3.9% annual
inflation. 
However, under the surface, the details were more concerning. Measure of core inflation have taken a
step higher, with several closely watched measures now at or slightly above the top of the RBNZ’s
target band. 
We suspect that today’s result will leave the market continuing to price a strong chance of another
OCR hike at next Wednesday’s policy review. In that light, we think the RBNZ will regard this as the
path of least resistance, and we now expect that they will deliver (previously we expected that they
would pause and assess, before hiking at the December MPS).

What contributed to inflation in the September quarter?
Underpinning September’s 0.7% rise in consumer prices were some big price movements in both
directions. 
The largest move in prices this quarter was actually a sharp fall in fuel costs. Fuel prices aren’t low by
any stretch of the imagination. However, average prices for both petrol and diesel over the September
quarter were lower than in the June quarter when prices rocketed higher in the wake of the Middle East

### Page 3

conflict. In terms of specifics, the average price for 91 unleaded was 6.5% lower in September than in
the June quarter, while diesel prices were close to 16% lower. Those moves took 0.4ppts off inflation
this quarter. 
While prices at the pump weren’t as high as they were in the June quarter, fuel costs are still painfully
high. And that’s been bleeding through into higher prices for other goods and services. Of note, the
September quarter saw large increases in passenger transport costs, with international airfares up 14%
and domestic airfares up nearly 8%. 
The September quarter also saw the annual increases in local council rates (up 6.2%) and charges for
services like water supply (up 7.5%). That continues the run of large increases seen in recent years.
Lastly, the past few months saw a 1.0% rise in food prices, largely as a result of the seasonal rise in
prices for fresh vegetables. 
On the downside, we’ve seen continued softness in housing rents, which are the largest component of
the CPI, accounting for 11.2% of the basket. With low population growth and ample supply, rents were
flat in the September quarter and have effectively been flat since the start of this year. In annual terms,
rental inflation is the lowest it’s been in more than two decades, with regions like Wellington seeing
outright falls.

Annual and core inflation 
The annual inflation rate dropped back to 3.7% in the September quarter, down from 4.1% in the year
to June and the highest level in two years.
Looking under the surface, prices in the domestically oriented non-tradables group rose 1.0% over the
quarter, less than expected. That saw annual non-tradables inflation nudging down to 3.3% (from 3.4%
in the year to June). 
Non-tradables inflation has continued to run at above-average rates over the past year. That’s despite
the softness in economic growth and the labour market. In large part, that’s due to the continued
sizeable increases in administered prices, such as electricity charges which rose 9.3% over the past
year. 
However, prices in other areas have also been firm. Non-tradables excluding housing and utilities costs
(which also omits local council rates) was 3.4% for the year. In seasonally adjusted terms, quarterly
non-tradables inflation has been tracking around 0.8% for most of the past year. It was noted that in
sectors like construction, higher materials costs are adding to prices. Feedback from business we've
heard indicates that those higher materials costs are likely related to high oil prices. 
On the imported front, lower fuel costs saw tradable prices rising by just 0.2% over the September
quarter (though above our forecast for a small fall). That saw annual tradables inflation dropping back
to 4.3%, down sharply from the 4.9% rise in the year to June. 
While fuel costs have been a key driver for tradables inflation, under the surface, other imported
inflation pressures are looking firm. Excluding food and fuel costs, tradables prices were up 2.7% over
the past year. That’s the highest level in three years. 
With big swings in fuel costs, and concern that this is spilling over into operating costs more generally,
a key focus for the RBNZ is what’s been happening to measures of core inflation (which smooth
through quarter-to-quarter swings in individual prices and instead track the underlying trend in

### Page 4

Related articles
inflation). 
On this front we did some see worrying signs. Several closely watched measures of core inflation have
picked up, and now sit at the top of (or slightly above) the RBNZ target band. In terms of specifics, we
saw: 
Reinforcing this picture of firm underlying inflation pressures, a growing number of goods have been
increasing in price. That could be an early indication that businesses, even those with a limited
exposure to fuel costs, are starting to factor in expectations of continued high inflation when setting
prices.

Outlook 
While today’s result was lower than the RBNZ assumed in their September MPS projections, the
firmness in core inflation will give the RBNZ pause for thought ahead of their policy review on 28
October. Furthermore, with a sharp rise in petrol prices in recent weeks, September’s easing in annual
inflation is likely to be just a temporary reprieve. We expect headline inflation to reaccelerate back over
4% before the end of this year, and it’s set to remain above the RBNZ’s current forecast for most of
2027. 
Market pricing and views have coalesced around an October hike which we now suspect the MPC will
see as the path of least resistance. Core inflation measures are now close to or above 3%, which will
add fuel to arguments from the MPC hawks. We will have more detail in our MPR Preview later today,
including on the implications for the shape of the tightening cycle moving forward.

European gas prices climbed above EUR100/MWh as mounting
supply concerns rattle the market ahead of the 2026/27 winter
Warren Patterson
European natural gas prices rallied further yesterday, with TTF
settling 4.85% higher. Prices broke above EUR100/MWh for the ﬁrst
time since 2022. The market has moved higher, with little sign of
imminent relief in Persian Gulf LNG ﬂows. If anything, the outlook
appears more dire amid the risk of renewed US strikes on Iran

following the US midterm elections next week. Reportedly,
QatarEnergy has extended its force majeure for several buyers until
the end of the year. It means signiﬁcant LNG supply disruptions are
creeping deeper into the heating season. In addition, several
unplanned outages in Norway will add to supply concerns.
Furthermore, forecasts show colder-than-usual weather in
Northwest Europe from next week, pushing heating demand higher.
This will likely start leading to more sustained drawdowns in

storage. EU gas storage is just shy of 75% full. While we’ve had a

The key question is whether these higher prices will destroy

Chemical company Yara recently reported curtailments of
ammonia production in Europe due to high gas prices. This led the

Document 1371: What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it_ (2026-10-11)

Source PDF: all report pdf/What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it_ (2026-10-11).pdf
Report source: Unknown
Date: 未知日期
Pages: 17
Status: ok

### Page 1

1
EXPERT TAKE FOLLOW THE MONEY
What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it?
A closer look at the impact of China’s currency on China’s export growth.
Sean Yong/Reuters
UPDATED
October 11, 2026 12:00 a.m.
Articles Follow the Money Share
Log In
Regions Topics Research Experts Events The Future of American Strategy

### Page 2

2
Brad W. Setser CFR EXPERT
Whitney Shepardson Senior Fellow
There is an argument—made in the recent Geneva
Report and by various former IMF officials—that
China’s current export surge is the simple
consequence of the housing downturn and the
resulting weakness in Chinese internal demand.*
The weakness in the RMB in this story is entirely
incidental to the increase in exports, which is, more or
less, a mechanical response to weak internal demand.

Cannot sell excavators at home? Export them.
Built more modern car capacity than your internal
market supports? Export that too…
The fall in the nominal RMB over the course of 2022
and the first half of 2023 in nominal and read terms
was simply a function of domestic macroeconomic
weakness, and a growing rate differential. It wasn’t an
active policy choice by China’s central bank.

### Page 3

3
Now, some might note that China’s currency doesn’t
always move with rate differentials. The RMB didn’t
consistently get pulled up when Chinese rates were
higher than U.S. rates (2002-2020 generally
speaking), and while it did fall when rate differentials
moved against the RMB in 2022 and 2023, it then
stabilized and has even appreciated modestly since
the middle of last year. That appreciation hasn’t been
big enough to correct the deep undervaluation of the

RMB, but it came at a time when the PBOC policy
rate (the reverse repo rate) was well below the U.S.
policy rate.
China doesn’t have an open financial account. As a
result, equilibrium in the foreign exchange market is
thus driven far more by exporter conversion and
current account flows than by rate differentials and
financial flows.** That, together with China’s ongoing
management of the exchange rate and a trade surplus
that can generate significant inflows, means that the

### Page 4

4
value of the RMB is much more of a policy variable
under the independent control of the Chinese
authorities than a simple byproduct of monetary and
fiscal policies.
The modern IMF is reluctant to accept this
conclusion. Its surveillance has generally ignored
China’s currency management (even if that
management is relatively obvious; see the data on FX
settlement) and its recent comprehensive assessment
of China’s economy completely ignored the balance of

payments and exchange rate management.
But it is pretty obvious to the market, even if the
PBOC, rather absurdly, insists that “market forces
play a decisive role in determining the RMB
exchange rate.”
I doubt the PBOC can win this argument. I agree
with Mark Sobel:
“The renminbi is still heavily managed and the
authorities have acted to slow appreciation. The paper
states that the PBoC phased out ‘regular’ foreign
exchange intervention in 2017. But it has many

means at its disposal to achieve the same effect
through extensive capital controls, administrative
guidance, signalling at the fix and deploying state-
owned commercial banks. These means are heavily
used. Thus, the word ‘regular’ must be taken with a
pinch of salt. The comparison to Japan, which

### Page 5

5
intervenes occasionally, is spurious – the yen largely
floats freely in integrated global markets. The same
cannot be said for the renminbi.”
In reality, the PBOC’s daily fix now plays the decisive
role in the currency’s path, and the market is often a
bet on how the PBOC’s management of the yuan will
evolve.
That is clear from the lack of volatility in the yuan’s
rate against the dollar. The yuan’s move down against
the dollar in 2022 was a controlled 10 percent move,

and the appreciation over the last 16 months has been
even more controlled crawl.
And the market is clearly massaged with substantial
help from the state banks. In fact that the pattern of
changes in the monthly FX settlement data looks
exactly like the pattern of intervention of a central
bank managing its currency around a tight band (the

### Page 6

6
state banks in practice buy FX to keep the CNY from
testing the strong side of the band, so there is an
asymmetry in how the CNY is managed)
None of this would matter much if China’s economy
was small. But that obviously isn’t the case. Nor would
this matter much if China’s exports didn’t respond to
changes in the RMB’s real (and nominal) value. But
that is also not the case.
There is abundant evidence that China’s exports do
respond to moves in the currency. Periods of RMB

weakness have consistently been associated with
periods of especially rapid Chinese export growth.

### Page 7

7
Chancellor Merz and President Macron got this
right, even if macroeconomic issues haven’t yet
figured prominently in the EU’s dialogue with
China.*** As they note in their open letter to the
European Commission:
“An appreciation of undervalued currencies towards a value
more in line with fundamentals would help support the
rebalancing of trade accounts with the EU in the short and
medium term … European policy discussions focused on
forging a common understanding of these exchange rate issues

and their interaction with global imbalances would be useful.”
The best evidence that exports responded to changes
in the currency, and not simply to changes in the path
of China’s internal demand, is the acceleration in
China’s export growth after the RMB’s depreciation
over the course of 2022.
This is the killer chart.

### Page 8

8
Now, you might ask: what of the acceleration in
export growth in 2020 and 2021? That was pretty
clearly tied to the global increase in goods demand
that came with the pandemic and work from home
requirements. It was expected to fade when the world
economy normalized. But it didn’t. By 2023 Chinese
export growth again topped global trade growth.
The general expectation that the rise in China’s goods
surplus during Covid would prove to be “transitory”

### Page 9

9
heavily influenced the IMF’s work at the time: see the
IMF’s external sector reports of 2023 and 2024.
I would argue that neglecting the exchange rate was
the key reason the IMF’s kept forecasting, incorrectly,
that China’s current account surplus would fall (See
this blog with Shahin Vallee). The IMF certainly
didn’t warn that China’s property downturn and the
RMB’s real depreciation risked a second China shock
in its 2022, 2023, or 2024 surveillance reports.

Concretely, the weaker RMB appears to have
contributed to a very large outperformance of China’s
exports relative to global trade. See the following
chart
That incidentally also happened after the RMB
followed the dollar down in 2003.
In both periods, there were significant structural
shifts. The WTO accession in 2002, and the success

### Page 10

10
of Chinese industrial policies in the “green” industrial
sectors and autos in 2022. In both cses exports were
turbocharged when structural shifts that should have
resulted in a stronger currency were instead amplified
by currency weakness.
No matter. Paul Krugman has noted that a country
that is converging technologically with its trade
partners should see a trend appreciation in its
currency. China got the technological convergence,
but not the real appreciation—at least not until this

year. And the move since the middle of 2025 has
corrected the depreciation of the RMB that occurred
when the RMB followed the dollar down on
liberation day, but not the structural overvaluation.
Now, there is an argument that exchange rate
adjustment is too hot an issue to make it a priority.
The PBOC isn’t interested it seems.
And some believe that in the interest of comity and
good relations with China, the IMF should mirror
the PBOC’s views. After all a stronger RMB would

slow China’s exports and thus slow China’s economy
at a time when China needs export growth to escape
deflation and generate employment. Or so the
argument goes. Concerns about “external balance“
and the negative global spillovers from China’s rising
goods surplus should be ignored and the Fund’s sole
focus should be on policies that lead to internal

### Page 11

11
balance. That provides one rationale for the Fund’s
ongoing decision to essentially ignore the contentious
issue of the PBOC’s ongoing exchange rate
management.
That argument, however, assumes that China’s
economy is small and thus China’s external surplus
can safely be ignored because it isn’t a drag on the
growth of the IMF’s other members.
That clearly isn’t true.
And it isn’t clear that China is more interested in
having a negotiation over its level of basic pension

benefits or the size of its fiscal deficit (where the
IMF continues to make timid recommendations that
would not move the needle—and certainly wouldn’t
meaningfully reduce China’s external surplus) than a
discussion over its currency practices.****
Back in the world of fixed but adjustable exchange
rates, there was an expectation (not always met to be
sure) that surplus countries would allow their
currencies to strengthen to bring their economies

back into external balance, and that other policy tools
would be used to ensure internal balance.
I would argue that China’s exchange rate (against
both the dollar and the basket) has many similarities
to the old world of fixed but adjustable currencies.
True, it moves on a controlled path when it moves

### Page 12

12
between different levels rather than jumping up and
down. But the PBOC does frequently target a level,
and that targeted level does change over time.
I would further argue that steps like the recent tariff
rate quota that will limit China’s exports of hybrid
cars to Europe to around 350,000 units next year (up
from 2025, but well below the 800,000 units of
2026) aren’t going to address the underlying
imbalance on their own. They can provide a bit of a

buffer for specific sectors.
But that buffer, while necessary, won’t address the
broad-based erosion of manufacturing capacity
outside China. This erosion will persist as long as an
undervalued RMB sends the entire world a signal to
use China as its production base.
The new system of managed trade that is emerging in
autos would need to be progressively expanded to an
ever-increasing set of sectors if protection is used as a
substitute for both domestic reform in China and

exchange rate adjustment.
That is now the direction of travel, but it doesn’t
address the underlying systemic issues.
Incidentally, those who believe the path of internal
demand is critical to rebalancing and that exchange
rate moves are secondary need to explain how an
acceleration in domestic demand would, on its own,

### Page 13

13
lead China’s external accounts to adjust. One
important, stylized fact about China is that domestic
demand growth is no longer feeding over to import
growth (ex-gold, that is).
Bottom line: China, which needs a 1.5 percentage
point contribution from net exports every year, is on a
collision course with its trading partners without a
currency correction that provides the basis for more
balanced trade even in the absence of trade
restrictions.
And there isn’t a realistic path towards balance that

doesn’t involve a stronger RMB; there aren’t, as Paul
Krugman once put it, immaculate transfers.
* That downturn shows up in domestic deflationary
pressure, and weak job growth/high rates of (at least
youth) unemployment. China, in other words, isn’t in
“internal balance.” I really liked the report from

### Page 14

14
Kamakshya Trivedi and Hui Shan of Goldman Sachs
arguing China needs two tools to hit two targets
(internal and external balance).
** To be sure, rate differentials matter for exporter
conversion—but so does the expected movement of
the RMB. The market understands this better than
the Fund. The Chen and Suwanapruti (Goldman
Sachs) note uses a framework similar to mine to
describe the CNY’s moves in Q3:
“In our view, sizeable FX inflows have continued to support

RMB appreciation despite unfavorable interest rate
differentials, as strong export receipts and increased exporter
FX conversions have outweighed portfolio outflows. Our
estimated FX conversion ratio rose to 63% in August,
compared with around 45% in normal years, likely reflecting a
shift in market expectations from RMB depreciation to
appreciation.”
*** Š ef č ovi č  has jurisdiction over trade policy
(narrowly defined), but not broader macroeconomic

policies. Europe’s institutional architecture for
exchange rate coordination is not well-developed.
**** The current account surplus is no longer masked
to the same extent as in 2023 and 2024, as SAFE has
fiddled with its BoP methodology once again (per the
Federal Reserve) and the BoP goods surplus is no
longer significantly below the customs goods surplus.
Of course, there are still problems in the data—the
deficit in the investment income account most

（2020年 = 100）

2026 年 10 月 5 日

調査レポート

今月のグラフ（2026 年 10 月）

制度変更が押し上げた耐久財需要

調査部 研究員 小林 啓介

2026 年 4～6 月期の実質 GDP における個人消費は前期比＋0.0%と横ばいにとどまったものの、耐久財は同
＋4.0%と堅調に増加した。特に自動車とエアコンの需要が大きく高まったことが、押し上げに寄与したとみられる。 
新車販売台数（除く軽）は、自動車の燃費性能に応じて取得時に課税される「環境性能割」が 2025 年度末に
廃止されることを受けて今年度に需要の一部が先送りされた結果、4 月に前月比＋25.7%と急増した。同様にエ
アコンの出荷台数も、2027 年度から省エネ基準が厳しくなり、製品価格の上昇が予想されることから、それ を見
越した駆け込み需要が生じ、4 月には前月比＋12.5%と急増した。 
もっとも、こうした制度・規制変更に起因する一時的な需要増は徐々に落ち着きつつある。自動車とエアコンは
いずれも依然として高水準ではあるものの、4 月をピークに減少傾向に転じている。雇用・所得環境は良好であり、
イラン情勢悪化の影響で落ち込んでいた 消費者マインドも持ち直しへ向かっているなど、 個人消費を取り巻く環
境は悪くない。このため、7～9 月期の個人消費は底堅く推移するとみられるものの、耐久財消費の一時的な押し
上げ効果が剥落することで、小幅な伸びにとどまる可能性があることには注意を要しよう。

才能出炉。
此次选举被⼴泛视为对内塔尼亚胡执政的⼀次公投。这场选举是 2023 年 10 ⽉ 7 ⽇哈⻢斯主导的加
沙袭击事件爆发、以⾊列陷⼊⻓达三年战争以来的⾸次议会选举，选⺠情绪⾼度对⽴。
出⼝⺠调： “ 反内塔尼亚胡 ” 阵营预计领先，阿拉伯政党 “ 异军突起 ”
根据以⾊列第 13 频道电视台出⼝⺠调，内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团预计获得 25 席，位列第
⼀； Eisenkot 领导的中间派政党正直党（ Yashar ）预计获得 22 ⾄ 23 席，位列第⼆；前总理
Naftali Bennett 领导的团结党预计获得 14 席，位列第三。
从阵营划分来看， Eisenkot 领导的反内塔尼亚胡阵营预计获得 53 席，内塔尼亚胡领导的右翼宗
教政党阵营预计获得 50 席，双⽅均未达到组建多数派政府所需的 61 席。如果⽬前的㬵着局⾯持

续下去，内塔尼亚胡的命运将取决于以⾊列总统是否⾸先给予他或 Eisenkot 组建⾄少 61 席议会
多数派的机会。
阿拉伯裔政党的表现是本次选举最⼤的意外。出⼝⺠调显⽰，阿拉伯裔政党联盟 " 联合名单 " 预计
获得 10 席，阿拉伯各党合计席位有望达到 17 ⾄ 18 席，创历史新⾼。以媒分析认为，阿拉伯裔政
党在未来组阁谈判中的重要性将进⼀步凸显。
《以⾊列时报》指出，反对派阵营内部存在严重分歧，尤其是在是否与阿拉伯政党合作的问题
上，这可能阻碍其将选举优势转化为执政联盟。值得注意的是，以⾊列没有地理选区，整个国
家作为单⼀选区运作，选⺠从相同的政党名单中进⾏选择。
组阁路径复杂，再次⼤选⻛险犹存

### Page 4

中的任何意⻅、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任⾃负。
315 收藏 分享到 :
写评论
图⽚
据 CNN 报道，最终计票结果出炉后，以⾊列总统 Herzog 将启动⼀轮磋商，听取各当选政党对总
理⼈选的推荐，再据此授权最有可能成功组阁的候选⼈进⾏谈判。获授权者将有四⾄六周时
间，就内阁职位、预算优先事项及政策⽅向与各党展开谈判，⼒求在议会中凑⾜多数。
就⽬前形势⽽⾔，由于反对派阵营和阿拉伯政党均不会推荐内塔尼亚胡，总统 Herzog ⼤概率将
⾸先授权 Eisenkot 组阁。希伯来⼤学 aChord 中⼼当晚进⾏的调查显⽰，多数反对派阵营选⺠⽀
持 Eisenkot 与阿拉伯政党之⼀ Raam 合作组建政府。
然⽽， Eisenkot 作为政坛新⼈，组阁失败的可能性真实存在。⼀旦失败，总统将转⽽授权另⼀候
选⼈ —— 很可能是内塔尼亚胡 —— 再次尝试。若两轮均告失败，议会将获得⼀个短暂窗⼝期⾃

⾏提名候选⼈，若仍⽆果，以⾊列将再次举⾏⼤选。
就像 2019 年那样，各党派领导⼈组阁尝试失败的可能性始终存在，这将导致议会解散并再次举
⾏⼤选。到 2022 年，在 Bennett- 拉⽪德政府垮台后，以⾊列已举⾏了不下五次⼤选。此次选举
结果若最终⽆法形成稳定联合政府，以⾊列政坛的这⼀历史轮回或将再度上演。
内塔尼亚胡⾯临政治⽣涯最艰难挑战
以⾊列任期最⻓的领导⼈内塔尼亚胡断断续续担任总理近⼆⼗年，如今正⾯临政治⽣涯中最严
峻的考验。他因 2023 年 10 ⽉ 7 ⽇以⾊列安全体系的重⼤失守，以及此后加沙战争的处置⽅式，承
受着来⾃国内外的巨⼤压⼒。
内塔尼亚胡此前曾多次从丑闻、选举失利和腐败指控中东⼭再起，但从未遭遇过如此直接冲击
其 " 以⾊列最强安全守护者 " 这⼀核⼼政治标签的打击。

2023年 2024年 2027年2026年2025年
１. 東南アジア５カ国の経済は、2026 年 4-6 月期も底堅く推移したが、成長率の差が鮮明に
なった。外需では半導体・電子関連需要を背景に電気電子製品を中心とする輸出が景気
を支え、内需でも消費や投資、政府支出が下支えした。一方、物価高や公共投資の停滞
が重石となる国もあり、各国の成長格差が広がった。

２. 消費者物価は足元で上昇し、フィリピンやベトナムを中心にインフレ圧力が強まってい
る。先行きは、中東情勢悪化による原油高やエルニーニョの強まりを背景に、2027 年初
まで物価上昇圧力が根強く残ろう。その後は供給制約の緩和や前年の反動から多くの国
で鈍化するものの、 原油・食品価格の不確実性は大きく、 再加速リスクに注意を要する。

３. 金融政策は、2026 年にフィリピンとインドネシアが物価高や通貨安を受けて利上げに転
じた。先行きは、原油高や食品高、米 FRB の 9 月利上げによる通貨安圧力から高金利が
長期化し、両国は年内、マレーシアは 2027 年初に利上げを予想する。2027 年後半は物
価・通貨安圧力の緩和に伴い、フィリピンとインドネシアは利下げに転じよう。

４. 先行きは、AI・半導体関連の輸出や投資が景気を下支えする一方、物価高や高金利、政
策執行の違いから成長格差が続く見通しである。マレーシアは内外需 、インドネシアは
内需に支えられて底堅く、ベトナムは輸出・投資をけん引役に高成長を維持し、フィリ
ピンは公共投資の正常化から 2027 年に持ち直す一方、 タイは家計部門の弱さから力強さ
を欠こう。中東情勢や米国の通商政策、エルニーニョは ASEAN の下振れリスクとなる。 
東南アジア経済の見通し  
～AI・半導体関連需要が成長を下支えも、 
物価高と高金利が重石

### Page 2

（物価：インフレ圧力が再び強まるも、2027 年は鈍化へ） 
東南アジア５カ国の消費者物価上昇率は、2026 年に入り総じて上昇傾向にある（図表２） 。エネ
ルギー価格の上昇に加え、食品価格の上昇が物価を押し上げており、年央以降はフィリピンやベ
トナムを中心にインフレ圧力が強まっている。一方、マレーシアでは物価上昇率が低位にとどま
るなど、国ごとの差も大きい。 
直近の消費者物価上昇率をみると、フィリピンは 8 月に前年同月比 6.1％と５カ国で最も高く、
ベトナムも同 4.9％まで上昇した。インドネシアは同 3.2％、タイは同 2.5％と上昇している一
方、マレーシアは 7 月に同 1.8％と低水準にとどまった。フィリピンではコメなど食品価格やエネ

### Page 3

（金融政策：利下げ局面は一巡、引き締め姿勢を維持） 
東南アジア５カ国の金融政策は、2025 年か
ら続いた利下げ局面が概ね一巡し、2026 年は
物価高や通貨安への対応から一部の国で引き締
め方向に転じている。中東情勢を背景とする原
油価格の上昇や食品価格の上振れに加え、国際
金融市場の不透明感も続いており、各国中央銀
行は景気への配慮を残しつつ、物価・為替の安
定を重視する姿勢を強めている。 
国別にみると、インドネシア中銀は 5～6 月
に累計 1.0％ポイントの利上げを実施し、政策
金利を 5.75％とした。フィリピン中央銀行もインフレ再加速を受けて 4 月、6 月、8 月に各
0.25％ポイント利上げし、政策金利を 5.00％まで引き上げた。一方、マレーシア中銀は 2.75％、
タイ中銀は 2 月の利下げ後に 1.00％で据え置いており、ベトナム国家銀行もリファイナンスレー
トを 4.50％に維持している。このため、足元では引き締めに転じた国と据え置きを続ける国に政
策対応が分かれている。 
先行きは、中東情勢の再悪化に伴う原油高やエルニーニョによる食品価格上昇に加え、米国の
金融引き締め長期化も各国の政策運営を制約するとみられる。米 FRB は 9 月に利上げへ転じ、
2027 年も高い政策金利を維持する見通しを示しており、ドル高や資本流出を通じた通貨安圧力が
続けば、東南アジア各国でも高金利の維持が長期化しよう。インドネシアとフィリピンでは 2026
年末に追加利上げを予想し、マレーシアでも景気の堅調さを背景に 2027 年初に利上げするとみて
いる。一方、タイとベトナムは政策金利を据え置くと予想する。2027 年後半には物価・通貨安圧
力が和らぎ、インドネシアとフィリピンでは利下げに転じると予想する。

（経済見通し：外需は底堅いが、物価高・高金利が内需の重石に） 
東南アジア５カ国の経済は、2026 年後半から 2027 年にかけても総じて底堅い成長が続くとみら

樺漢(6414)  
- 樺漢營運雙引擎發力，實體AI與廠
務需求推升獲利成長  
投資建議 
標題  
 樺漢投資評等為買進，目標價 480 元，預估 2027 年 EPS 為 30.21 元，建議
在本益比 13-16 倍操作，主要理由如下： 
(1) 邊緣運算與廠務需求暢旺：前三季營運動能主要受惠於全球 Physical AI 
應用、AI 邊緣運算及半導體高科技廠務工程需求強勁，帶動工控與智慧廠務
出貨暢旺，使前三季累計營收達 1,349.4 億元，年增 31.3%。 
(2) 實體 AI 落地與廠務擴產：受惠於美洲 AI 資料中心與邊緣運算設備出貨放
量，加上歐洲 Kontron 整合效益持續發酵；配合全球半導體先進製程擴產潮
及 Physical AI 軟硬整合商機，推升營收與獲利結構穩健成長。   
內容摘要 
 前三季營收創新高，雙引擎驅動成長   
樺漢前三季累計營收達 1,349.4 億元（年增 31.3%），3Q26 單季營收 494.4
億元的歷史新高。三大事業群中，工控物聯網佔 45.7%、智慧工廠與廠務佔
42.6%、智慧軟體與方案佔 11.7%，在手訂單規模突破 2,550 億元，奠定穩
固基礎。   
  深耕實體AI轉型，擴展全球在地製造  
展望 2H26 及 2027 年，集團持續推動「Local-for-Local」在地化製造策
略，優化台灣高階樞紐並擴充歐美亞太產能。同時積極發展 Physical AI 軟硬
整合平台、機器人系統與 OT 資安訂閱制，全面深化全球關鍵場域佈局。   
   受惠AI邊緣運算與廠務工程需求  
成長動能主要來自全球 Physical AI 應用、AI 邊緣運算與美洲資料中心需求強
勁，帶動工控產品出貨暢旺；加上半導體先進製程與高科技廠務工程持續推
進，以及歐洲 Kontron 整合效益發酵，同步推升營收與獲利結構優化。

:: 訪談內容::

公司簡介 
 1. 樺漢科技為全球工業電腦與嵌入式系統廠，隸屬於鴻海集團，近年
營運重 心正由 傳統 低毛利 之硬體 製造， 加速 朝向高 附加價 值之
「ESaaS」軟硬體整合服務與 Physical AI 轉型。 
2. 集團最強勢之處在於具備龐大研發能量與鴻海採購資源，全球編制
逾 3,600 位工程師且年投百億研發費，並攜手 NVIDIA、聯發科切
入邊緣運算。  
3. 樺漢實施分散式全球在地製造與研發，研發重鎮有  40% 分佈於亞
太、50% 於歐洲、10% 於美洲，透過旗下子公司 Kontron 深耕歐
美市場，結合亞太製造資源以強化全球供應鏈韌性。

產品組合 
 1. 3Q26 產品組合：工控物聯網 (占比 45.7%)、智慧軟體與方案 (占比
11.7%)及智慧工廠與廠務(占比 42.6%)。 
2. 工 控 物 聯 網 ：3Q26 受 惠 於 全 球 Physical AI 應 用 與 AI Edge 
Computing 需求強勁，帶動出貨暢旺；2026 年持續受惠於 AI 邊緣
運算與智慧工廠升級擴展，推動營收與高附加價值業務穩健成長。  
3. 智 慧 軟 體 與 方 案 ：3Q26 持 續 深 化 高 附 加 價 值 與 經 常 性 收 入
（ARR），強化資安與智慧平台應用；2026 年預期軟體與解決方案
比重將進一步拉升，推動獲利結構優化與長期客戶黏著度。 
4. 智慧工廠與廠務：3Q26 在智慧資安、交通、航太與半導體高科技廠
務工程持續推進下表現穩健；2026 年受惠於半導體擴產與全球智慧
製造升級潮，帶動整合系統與自動化供應系統持續高成長。 
5. 3Q26 年各應用營收占比：工控物聯網 45.7%、智慧軟體與方案
11.7%及智慧工廠與廠務 42.6%。 
6. 預估 2026 年各應用營收占比：工控物聯網 44%、智慧軟體與方案
15%及智慧工廠與廠務 41%。

營運狀況 
 1. 3Q26 營收 494.4 億元，YoY+47.1%，3Q26 營運動能變化的主要
原因是受惠於美洲 AI 資料中心與邊緣運算設備出貨暢旺，加上歐洲
Kontron 整合效益發酵，帶動單季獲利與營收同步創高。 
2. 前三季累計營收 1,349.4 億元，YoY+31.3%，前 3 季營運動能變化
主要受惠於全球 Physical AI 應用、AI 邊緣運算及半導體高科技廠務
工程需求強勁，帶動工控與智慧廠務出貨暢旺。 
3. 2026 年營收與全年展望、Physical AI 策略與市場，以及 Kontron 整
合效益。三大主題為投資人勾勒出樺漢由營運實績邁向實體  AI 轉型
的清晰藍圖。 
4. 前三季三大事業群營收：工控物聯網 616.8 億(45.7%)、智慧軟體
158.3 億(11.7%)、智慧工廠 574.2 億元(42.6%)，在手訂單超 2,550
億元。 
5. Physical AI 具備感知與行動能力，市場 10 年成長超 20 倍達 1,200 
億美元，樺漢積極布局並設定 3 億美元目標市佔。 
6. 公司  2026 年 9 月 營 收 177.55 億元， MoM +14.65% 、 YoY 
+45.34%，累計月營收 1,349.4 億元，YoY+31.3%。 
7. 全球生產基地積極推動「 Local-for-Local」在地化製造策略，台灣
廠作為研發與高階製造樞紐，並優化歐洲與亞美生產據點，降低地
緣政治與供應鏈波動風險。 
8. 積極發展 Physical AI 軟硬整合平台、機器人系統（AMR 與人形機器
人）及 OT 資安軟體訂閱制服務，各項新產品與平台已順利導入全球
關鍵場域。 
9. AI 需求正從雲端生成式 AI 快速擴展至邊緣運算與實體 AI（Physical 
AI），應用場景涵蓋智慧工廠、物流與商業服務，需求具備高度持
續性與長期成長潛力。

### Page 4

未來展望  
 1. 預期 2026 年營收會有高成長，在工控物聯網與智慧工廠雙引擎帶
動下，呈現營收獲利雙高成長態勢。 
2. 2026 年財務目標動能源自高毛利 ESaaS 與 Physical AI 比重提
升，配合逾 2,550 億元在手訂單，確保長線毛利率穩步擴張。 
3. AI 應用擴展：AI 邊緣運算、生成式 AI 與雲端應用擴大，推動工業
設備從傳統運算載體轉型為高附加價值的智慧平台與實體 AI 應
用。 
4. 半導體擴產：受惠先進製程、先進封裝及 AI 基礎建設的長期投資
熱潮，帶動半導體高科技廠務工程與自動化供應系統強勁需求。 
5. 全球市場布局：樺漢持續深化全球在地化服務、強化供應鏈韌性，
並積極拓展海外新市場與新客戶，提升國際接單競爭力與長線空
間。 
6. Kontron 整合戰略著重歐洲與全球在地化製造，補完 AI 基礎設
施，建構完整 Physical AI 價值鏈 (AI 基礎設施 -> Edge AI -> 
Physical AI)。 
7. 2H26 及 2027 年公司積極推動「Local-for-Local」在地化製造策
略，優化台灣研發與高階製造樞紐，並擴充歐洲匈牙利、捷克、保
加利亞及越南、北美等區域化生產與交付中心，以降低地緣政治風
險。 
8. 2H26 及 2027 年積極發展 Physical AI 軟硬整合平台、機器人系統
（AMR 與人形機器人）及 OT 資安軟體訂閱制服務，各項新產品
與平台已順利導入全球關鍵場域。

工控物聯網業務 
 1. 預估 2026 年工控物聯網產品比重營收佔比 44%，不僅提供了穩定
的營運現金流，是引領實體 AI 技術商業化落地的重要關鍵。 
2. 隨著全球 AI 邊緣運算與邊緣智慧設備需求爆發，工控物聯網為占比
最高之業務，在 3Q26 展現強勁出貨動能，推動整體營收規模穩步
擴張。 
3. 樺漢積極切入 Physical AI 應用場景，將傳統工控設備升級為具備感
知與自主行動能力的智慧平台，帶動高附加價值產品比重持續提
升。 
4. 結合集團在工業電腦領域的深厚技術底蘊與全球在地化交貨能力，
工控物聯網在智慧工廠與智慧製造升級潮中取得顯著的市佔擴張優
勢。

金融支持三大国际科技创新中心建设的政策亮点 
技术研究部|李喆 赵艺苑 2026 年10 月 27 日

摘要： 
2026 年 10 月，中国人民银行等十一部门联合印发《关于金融支持建设北京（京
津冀） 、 上海 （长三角） 、 粤港澳大湾区国际科技创新中心的指导意见》 ， 围绕三大国际
科技创新中心建设部署 19 项工作举措，明确 2030 年和 2035 年两阶段目标，统筹贷
款、股权、债券、跨境金融四条线，对三地给出差异化定位。本文从金融服务与债券
市场视角出发，梳理《意见》的五大亮点：锚定科创资源禀赋推进区域差异化布局、
创新多维评价政策摆脱重资产重抵押依赖、打通信息共享堵点疏通成果转化链条、补
强债券市场工具链完善科创融资渠道、升级园区服务功能打造科技金融节点。这些安
排从区域协同、评价创新、信息共享、成果转化、债券融资和园区服务等层面，改善
了科技型企业的创新环境和金融服务可得性，有助于提升科技创新的资源配置效率。
其中，与信息获取、债券市场等相关的内容，也为评级机构改善信息基础、拓展评价
维度提供了条件。 
关键词：科技金融；国际科技创新中心；科创债；区域协同

正文： 
2026 年 10 月 19 日， 中国人民银行等十一部门联合印发了 《关于金融支持建设北
京 （京津冀） 、 上海 （长三角） 、 粤港澳大湾区国际科技创新中心的指导意见》 （以下简
称《意见》 ） ，围绕三大国际科技创新中心建设部署19 项工作举措，明确 2030 年和
2035 年两阶段目标， 旨在统筹区域协同、 机构协同与市场协同， 构建与科技创新全生
命周期相适应的金融服务体系。 
一、政策概述 
《意见》以 2025 年中央经济工作会议关于建设三大国际科技创新中心的部署为
背景， 提出19 项工作举措， 旨在推动京津冀、 长三角、 粤港澳大湾区打造科技金融协

### Page 2

政策解读| 专题研究
2 / 8
同发展高地。 《意见》 的总体定位， 是在京津冀、 长三角、 粤港澳大湾区三个已经具备
科创资源集聚度的区域，率先构建一套与“国际科技创新中心”定位相匹配的科技金
融服务体系。
《意见》明确了两阶段目标：到 2030 年，构建与国际科技创新中心相适应的科
技金融服务体系，支持科技创新全链条金融服务体系更加健全，直接融资占比明显提
升， 金融机构服务科技创新的专业能力显著提升， 区域金融服务一体化格局基本形成，
科技金融改革创新取得重要突破，对外开放水平持续提升；到 2035 年，建成与具有
全球影响力的国际科技创新中心相适应的科技金融体制， 实现直接融资与间接融资协
调并举、金融供给与科技创新需求高度适配、国际竞争力和影响力明显提升，科技金
融生态进一步优化，发挥引领示范作用，助力科技强国和金融强国目标实现。
《意见》统筹运用贷款、股权、债券、跨境金融四条线。贷款端将研发投入水平
较高的民营中小企业纳入科技创新和技术改造再贷款支持范围； 股权端强调壮大耐心

资本、发挥国家创业投资引导基金和社保科创基金作用；债券端聚焦科创债产品创新
与风险分担工具；跨境端则指向合格境外有限合伙人便利化、外债额度优化和“玉兰
债” “上海自贸离岸债”等通道。在统一框架之下， 《意见》对三地分别给出了差异化
定位，进行“定制化”布局，使金融资源投放与区域创新禀赋形成匹配：北京（京津
冀）聚焦原始创新和重大科技基础设施，上海（长三角）立足产业集群协同和共建共
享的科技金融生态，粤港澳大湾区侧重开放型科技金融体系和粤港澳规则对接。
二、政策亮点
《意见》 内容覆盖面较广， 从金融服务与债券市场视角出发，梳理以下五大亮点：
试点区域的选择与差异化布局、评价体系向人才创新能力延伸、公共信息跨区域共享
与科技成果转化机制、债券市场工具链补强与跨境通道延伸、科创园区向科技金融服
务节点转型。具体为：
（一）锚定科创资源禀赋，推进区域差异化布局
在科技创新中心建设方面，并非各地平均用力，而是依托创新资源密度较高、金
融服务能力较强、 产业链配套较完善的地区先行先试， 再通过区域协同机制向外传导。

《意见》 将政策效力集中于北京 （京津冀） 、 上海 （长三角） 、 粤港澳大湾区三个区域，
对其赋予差异化的功能定位，使金融资源投放与区域创新禀赋形成匹配。北京（京津
冀）具备基础研究、原始创新和总部经济优势；上海 （长三角）具备国际金融中心、
技术创新与高端产业协同优势；粤港澳大湾区具备产业集群、成果转化和跨境要素流

### Page 3

政策解读| 专题研究 
 3 / 8 
动优势。三地科技资源禀赋不同，决定了金融支持不能采取同一模板，而应形成差异
化、互补性的区域科技金融体系。 
从科技创新债券发行实践看，北京（京津冀） 、上海（长三角） 、粤港澳大湾区三
个区域恰好也是科技创新债券发行相对活跃的区域。2026 年前三个季度， 科技创新债
券发行高度集中于北京、广东、上海等地，京沪粤三地科创债发行数量、规模合计占
比分别达34.17%、49.60%， 其中，北京以 11,128.02 亿元的规模居全国首位， 占全国
总量的31.97%， 广东、 上海分别位列第三、第六位。 科技创新债券的发行与区域的科
技资源密度、 金融基础设施成熟度以及发行人群体厚度密不可分， 北京 （京津冀） 、 上
海 （长三角） 、 粤港澳大湾区三个区域经济基础雄厚， 金融基础设施完善， 科技创新活
跃且发行人群体聚集，科创债发行规模位居全国前列。

价重心转向“软实力”。《意见》明确提出“在依法合规、风险可控前提下，引导有条
件的金融机构完善信用评价体系， 将人才创新能力作为授信参考” ，也提出 “构建跨区
域科技金融服务联盟，在有效防范交叉性金融风险前提下，引导银行、证券、保险、
创业投资、担保、租赁等机构加强合作，探索完善服务模式，构建重大科技攻关项目

风险共担模式，协同做好科技型企业金融服务，为重大科技项目、产业链上下游和科
技成果异地转化提供金融支持” 。
上述政策的核心，是引导金融机构创新评价，打破传统金融评价中对固定资产和
抵押担保的依赖，将评价的重心向人才、技术、创新潜力等迁移。这是由于，科技型
企业核心资产往往表现为专利、技术秘密、研发团队、数据资源、软件著作权和尚未
形成规模收入的创新成果 ，此类资产价值波动大、变现周期长、 知识产权风险较高。
按照传统金融机构侧重资产、收入、利润、偿债等财务性指标，以及固定资产抵质押
的逻辑，科技型企业融资较为困难。将人才创新能力纳入授信参考，有助于识别企业
持续研发和组织迭代能力，但也要求金融机构建立可验证、可比较、可更新的评价维
度，防止“人才标签”流于形式。对评级机构而言，这意味着评级要素需要由静态财
务分析向创新能力、人才储备、技术实力等方面延伸，更加考验分析时的行业储备和
专家意见；重大科技攻关项目风险共担模式则要求重点识别风险承担主体、 补偿顺序、

追偿机制和损失分担比例。
（三）打通信息共享堵点，疏通成果转化链条
在跨区域协同部分，分别就公共信息跨区域共享和科技成果转化作出专门安排 ，
这两项内容在文件中各有独立段落， 指向的正是科技型企业融资实践中长期存在的两
个堵点，疏通信息链条将为评级机构提供更加全面、完善、公允的评价基础，有助于
更为公允地揭示科技型企业的优势与风险。
公共信息跨区域共享机制方面， 《意见》提出“建立科技公共信息跨区域共享机
制” ， 推动 “创新积分制” 在京津冀、 长三角、 粤港澳大湾区率先实现互联互通互认，
并引导征信机构加强科技公共信息采集运用， 建设科技型企业数据库。 在现有实践中，
科技型企业的评价模型已向研发投入、技术实力、创新成果转化 等非财务信息倾斜，
但部分科技领域数据信息不易获取， 且技术相关的信息分散在科技、 工信、 知识产权、
人社、金融监管等多个部门，标准不一、口径割裂，跨区域调取和互认的障碍尤为突
出，评级机构以及其他金融授信机构获取信息的覆盖面和可验证性受限。创新积分制
互认和公共信息跨区域共享机制的建立， 一方面有助于降低授信机构的数据获取难度、

改善对跨区域经营科技企业的信息获取质量， 降低因数据割裂而产生的评级不一致性，
另一方面，也为创新能力评价提供了一个潜在的公共数据接口。
科技成果转化机制方面， 《意见》提出“健全促进成果转化的金融服务模式” ，加
强科技成果研发地、 中试地、 产业转化地金融服务的衔接联动， 依托中国技术交易所、

上海技术交易所、深圳证券交易所科交中心等平台，探索科技成果资产确权、评估、
质押、 处置全链条服务机制， 推动三大技术交易所与国家统一技术交易服务平台互联，
完善科技成果价值评估与流转交易互认互通机制。科技型企业的专利技术、中试成果
等资产缺乏公允的估值参照，质押后处置路径不清晰，资产对债权的覆盖程度难以量
化。成果转化机制的推进，指向的是为科技资产建立可重复使用的价格参照和流转规
则，使金融机构在分析资产质量时，有条件从简单的“看专利数量”转向“看交易平
台上的评估与流转” 。 
（四）补强债券市场工具链，完善科创融资渠道 
《意见》对债券市场的部署，按照“发挥债券市场服务科技创新效能”的总体要
求， 从产品创新、 风险分担、 增信机制、 评级标准几个层面展开， 并延伸至 “玉兰债”
等对外开放通道。 
从境内市场看， 《意见》明确支持科技创新债券产品创新，“鼓励应用信用风险缓
释工具 （CRMW）、 信用保护工具等支持科技创新债券发行和投资”，“用好科技创新与民
营企业债券风险分担工具， 为符合条件的民营科技型企业和私募股权投资机构发债融
资提供担保增信”；“鼓励地方建立科技创新债券发行综合服务窗口，配套宣传路演和
增信赋能等‘一站式’服务”； 同时提出 “支持研究制定科技创新债券信用评级行业标
准” 。债券市场“科技板”自2025 年 5 月落地以来，市场规模扩张速度可观，正式推
出一年内， 债券市场已累计发行科创债2,336 只， 发行规模达25,802.96 亿元； 其中，
2026 年 1-5 月，科创债发行数量、规模分别为692 只、7,373.44 亿元，与2025 年未
推出“科技板”相比，分别增长 58.35%、82.73%。但规模扩张并不自动等于信用风险
定价的成熟， 与科创债配套的CRMW（信用风险缓释凭证） 创设规模整体仍然有限。同
一期间内，使用过CRMW 的科创债发行主体为23 家， 占全部科创债发行主体的2.32%
1
，
且标的主体集中于 AA 及以上级别的制造业企业，对低级别、中小及早期科技型企业
的覆盖不足。与此同时， “政府引导+市场运作”的增信机制尚未完全落地，风险缓释
产品针对性不足，难以有效对冲科技型企业的信用风险，投资者参与意愿受限。《意
见》此次对于债市的安排也表明政策向“把风险分担工具做深、把增信机制做实、把
评级标准做细”倾斜。 
从对外开放看， 《意见》在跨境金融部分提出，支持符合条件的科技型企业通过

（五）升级园区服务功能，打造科技金融节点
《意见》 对科创园区提出了因地制宜发展符合区域特点的科技金融服务体系的新
要求。在北京（京津冀）方向，要求“聚焦打造世界级原始创新策源地和自主创新主
阵地，强化金融支持战略科技力量集群和重大科技基础设施建设 ”，发挥中关村科创
金融改革试验区示范引领作用，推动相关经验向雄安新区科创园区推广；在上海（长
三角）方向，要求“聚焦发挥长三角龙头带动作用，打造多方参与、共建共享的科技

金融服务生态， 深化资金链与创新链、 产业链、 人才链的融合” ； 在粤港澳大湾区方向，
要求“发挥‘深圳-香港-广州’科技创新集群引领作用，加强粤港澳三地金融高水平
互动和规则对接”。
这意味着科创园区的功能定位正在 升级，未来科创园区将不止于提供办公空间、
厂房租赁和物业服务， 还将延伸至创业孵化、 投融资对接、 知识产权服务、 融资租赁、
股权投资和产业链协同等领域。同时“因地制宜健全契合区域特点的科技金融服务体
系”的要求，与文件中关于跨区域服务联盟、科技金融综合服务平台和风险共担模式
的安排相互交织， 实际上为科技园区赋予了远超传统 “空间提供者” 角色的功能期待。
从实践层面来看， 这一转型已经在部分园区中显现出轮廓。《意见》中提到的中关
村科创金融改革试验区、G60 科创走廊区域、深圳光明科学城、东莞松山湖科学城、
广州南沙科学城等重点区域，已经逐步发展为规模更大、特色鲜明、以专业化服务为
主的非行政化科技园区， 承担产业孵化、 技术转化、 资本对接、 生态构建等关键职能。

例如：北京中关村科技园培育国家高新技术企业 2.08 万家、独角兽企业93 家，形成
高强度研发投入与浓厚创新氛围，同时，园区通过设立创业孵化器、众创空间、论坛
等创业服务和交流平台，为初创企业提供办公场地、设备设施、创业辅导、法律咨询
等全方位服务， 帮助降低创业门槛与成本， 提高创业成功率。苏州设立产业引导基金、
创新产业发展引导基金、苏州天使母基金等基金，吸引境内外社会资本参与，聚焦苏

三、结论与启示
《意见》是首个专门针对三大国际科技创新中心的系统性金融支持文件，标志着
科技金融从单点政策探索转向跨区域、跨工具的制度化推进，服务于科技强国和金融
强国目标。 对科技型企业而言， 融资环境将从单一信贷支持向覆盖研发、 中试、 转化、
产业化的全生命周期金融服务延伸，融资可得性和风险承载能力有望系统性改善。
从金融服务与债券市场视角看， 本文梳理的五大亮点只是 《意见》 内容的一部分，
但共同指向改善科技型企业信用分析条件，下一步，也应重点关注以下三方面：一是
探索进一步把科技型企业软实力纳入信用风险分析框架，将分析指标向创新能力、人
才储备、技术实力延伸，研发团队稳定性、技术路线可行性、知识产权质量等软信息
要找到可跟踪、可验证的观察口径，防止“人才标签”流于形式；二是利用数据共享
和成果转化的制度成果，创新积分跨区域互认、科技公共信息共享、技术交易平台的
评估与流转信号， 推动信用风险分析基础向 “公共数据基础设施+专业判断” 演进；三

是结合CRMW、 担保增信、 风险分担工具以及跨境发行结构， 持续完善科创债评级方法。
